plaintext.source: contemporary decipherment in the recipient's office

system.summary: Hanoverian French syllabic nomenclator of 863 numbered groups (blanks and 864-1000 are nulls), with homophones, officers' and place names, and control groups 'annulle' / 'repete la precedente'.
system.notes: Two-part code: numbered decoding table (pp. 390-391) and alphabetical encoding table (pp. 386-388) in Ms XXIII 1234:31,1. 172 'Duc' is used for 'du'.

prior_solution.where: Letter 2 only: a contemporary worksheet (p. 121) glossing its 34 groups, with errors and a skipped pair. Letter 1: none.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5.5 and posed the problem with /goal, pasting the catalogue entry. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: two transcription subagents for the key table

solution.what: While checking catalogue 346, fetched the two 1743 Ilten letters flagged 'Teilweise dechiffrierter Brief' (Ms XXIII 1234:29,2) from GWLB Kitodo.
Transcribed letter 1's 189 code groups (no decipherment on it) and letter 2's 34 groups with the p. 121 worksheet glosses.
Kalliope search 'Ilten Chiffre*': volume 1234:31,1 (1745/46) lists a 'Chiffre-Tabelle', pp. 386-391.
Fetched pp. 386-391: numbered decoding table 1-863 and alphabetical encoding table; transcribed the decoding side (two agents, 28 checks against the worksheet values).
Applied the table to letter 1: fluent French on forage and discipline, Du Pontpietin and Sommerfeldt; dateline 866.223 = [null] Londres.
Applied it to letter 2: the worksheet's values agree group for group; the key also restores 278.613 'quoique avec' and corrects 'in-tra-c-tion' to 'instruction'.
Re-read the gutter digits from a full-resolution crop: 51, 407, 59, 95, 70, 705 ('ce dernier point'); 75? stays open.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): ciphertext_feb26/mar29.txt and the decipherments in reading.md with the sign-by-sign decode_*_signs.txt; no key work claimed, key1743/ not linked.

Verification 5 (plain-bar rows): both letters had been scored on the shared reading.md (German clear text, translations, notes). Readings written out per letter: feb26_reading.md (French cipher run, plain 0.727, explicit 1.0) and mar29_reading.md (German sentence with three French runs, explicit 1.0, judged as a reader). Both keep read.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The key table sits in a different volume of the Ilten papers (Ms XXIII 1234:31,1, 1745/46); it was found through the catalogue and matched to the 1743 letters by the worksheet values of letter 2.
outcome.fraction_read_source: ciphertext_feb26.txt + ciphertext_mar29.txt: 223 code groups; not reading as sense: 283, 75?, 59 in letter 1

gaps.item: letter 1 p. 74: 283.75? before 'me' (last digit in the gutter)

outcome.notes: Letter 1 had no decipherment at all; letter 2's contemporary worksheet was incomplete and partly wrong.

credits.note: Chiffre-Tabelle in the Ilten papers (Ms XXIII 1234:31,1 pp. 386-391) and the office worksheet of letter 2

texts.label: Unsigned letter from London, 15/26 Feb 1743 (pp. 73-75)
texts.summary: Unsigned letter from London to Johann Georg von Ilten, Hanoverian lieutenant-general with the Pragmatic Army. The French cipher passage approves Du Pontpietin's instructions to Lieutenant-General Sommerfeldt about forage and asks that the troops eat up the forage in their quarters so the French find nothing if they quarter there after them.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1743 French: plain share is a bar too): both entries pointed at reading.md, which holds the two letters with German clear text, translations and group notes (plain 0.347, explicit 0.733 for the file). The French cipher run of this letter written out alone, feb26_reading.md: plain 0.727 (8/11), explicit 1.0; the misses are fourage/consument/subsistance (period words the list lacks) and the two marked holes r[?], [e]. Keeps read.

texts.label: Ernst von Steinberg, London, 29 Mar / 9 Apr 1743 (pp. 119-121)
texts.summary: German letter from Ernst von Steinberg to Ilten with three code runs: it encloses an extract of the instruction just sent to Lord Stair, to be used with the utmost secrecy among His Majesty's German generals. A contemporary worksheet (p. 121) glosses the groups, partly wrongly.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026: both entries pointed at the two-letter reading.md (plain 0.347, explicit 0.733). This letter is one German sentence in clear with three short French cipher runs (34 groups); written out as mar29_reading.md, clear text in ⟨ ⟩. No word list scores a German-French mixture (de: plain 0.333, explicit 1.0); read as a reader the sentence holds and every run reads in full with the key, confirmed by the contemporary worksheet on p. 121. Keeps read.
